description: Licence corpus for the Rust sysroot crates statically linked into ThirdParty/wireguard-core/build/LavaSecWGCore.xcframework. These are NOT Cargo-resolved dependencies — they are pulled in from the pinned toolchain's precompiled standard library, so they are absent from Cargo.lock and cargo-metadata cannot see them, which is why this corpus is committed rather than derived. They ARE written into third-party-notices-index.json: the generator appends these entries to the same crate array as the Cargo-resolved ones, so the index is the union of both and must not be read as Cargo-only.

vendoredCrates.note: Crates the pinned toolchain builds from a VENDORED source tree rather than in-tree, so every slice's archive carries /rust/deps/<crate>-<version> path records for them and their versions are provable from the committed binaries. Declared here rather than derived from those records, because the version gate needs an expectation INDEPENDENT of the evidence it is testing: deriving the expected set from the observations meant a crate that lost its markers in every slice simply dropped out of the expectation and went unchecked. Changing this list is a reviewable diff and is only legitimate as part of a toolchain bump — the pinned toolchain is recorded in `toolchain`/`rustcCommitHash` above, so a list that no longer matches the archives fails the gate in both directions: a declared crate missing from any slice, and an observed vendored crate absent from this list.

appliesTo.evidence: Each slice's liblavasec_wireguard_core.a has 450 `ar t` members (449 excluding __.SYMDEF). Every member name of the form <crate>-<16 hex>.* was matched against lib<crate>-<16 hex>.rlib in lib/rustlib/<target>/lib of the pinned toolchain. Exactly 19 crates match in every slice and the NAME set is identical across all three (the metadata hashes differ per target, as expected). Apple `nm` and `xcrun llvm-nm` cannot read these objects (LLVM-17 reader vs LLVM-21 fat-LTO bitcode); `ar t` was used.
appliesTo.note: 386 of the 450 `ar t` members per slice carry a crate name listed in sysroot-crates.json (384 once the two Cargo-resolved copies of libc and cfg_if are excluded), and 366 of those come from compiler_builtins alone, whose 144 C/asm objects carry bare-hash member names. The measured breakdown, with each definition, is in resolutionSummary.sysrootMemberCount.

generatedFrom.role: std-scoped copyright notices; supplied the in-tree licence basis and full verbatim texts for 5 of the 19
whole-toolchain copyright notices; supplied verbatim texts for 4 gap crates once library/Cargo.lock disambiguated their versions, plus the addr2line texts

AUTHORITATIVE version pins for the crates std was built against; obtained by installing the rust-src component for the pinned 1.94.0 toolchain (`rustup component add rust-src --toolchain 1.94.0-aarch64-apple-darwin`)
the only authentic licence text for compiler_builtins
declared SPDX expression and version for compiler_builtins
SPDX canonical texts (12 files) shipped by the toolchain; Apache-2.0.txt, MIT.txt, Unicode-3.0.txt and LLVM-exception.txt are referenced by this corpus
LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE and Cargo.toml, fetched only to confirm that the toolchain's addr2line-0.24.2 texts are byte-identical for 0.25.1 and that the SPDX expression is unchanged

requiredRustSrc.note: rust-src (library/Cargo.lock and the in-tree manifests) was installed for this task and is the authoritative source for the versions std was built against.

versionCouldOnlyComeFromLibraryCargoLock.note: These are the crates the shipped documents genuinely cannot pin: absent from COPYRIGHT-library.html and listed in COPYRIGHT.html at 2-5 candidate versions each (or, for addr2line, not at the linked version at all).

absentFromBothOutOfTreeLists.note: Named in neither COPYRIGHT-library.html's nor COPYRIGHT.html's out-of-tree package list, at any version. Both are in-tree crates and were resolved from the rust-src tree.

absentFromCopyrightLibraryHtmlOutOfTreeL.note: Of these, the eight rust-lang/rust in-tree crates (alloc, core, panic_abort, rustc_std_workspace_alloc, rustc_std_workspace_core, std, std_detect, unwind) are still covered by that document's 'In-tree files' section; only addr2line, adler2, memchr, miniz_oxide, object and compiler_builtins are uncovered by it entirely.

$comment: Measured with scripts/lib/ar-archive.mjs against the committed slices, not asserted.
The previous value (240 per slice) matched no definition of the count and is corrected here.
byInventoryName: every member whose crate name appears in sysroot-crates.json. This
includes the Cargo-resolved copies of libc and cfg_if, which share a name with a sysroot
crate and appear as separate members (the sysroot copy keeps a version string; the Cargo
copy does not, because strip = "debuginfo" removed its DWARF).
sysrootOnly: the same count with those two Cargo copies excluded.
compilerBuiltins is broken out because it alone is the large majority.

$copyrightNote: Entries are full notice lines, not bare holder names. The distinction matters: the shared
MIT body these packages cite is the SPDX TEMPLATE, carrying an unfilled
"Copyright (c) <year> <copyright holders>" placeholder, because that is how the toolchain
ships it. The filled holder therefore has to travel in the package stanza or it travels
nowhere, and MIT clause 1 requires it to accompany the binary.
"Copyright (c) The Rust Project Developers" is the form rust-lang/rust states in its own
LICENSE-MIT, and the same line the Cargo path already recovers from libc.
$licenseTextRolesNote: Per cited text: is it an ALTERNATIVE the licensor offers (a disjunct, e.g. MIT OR Apache-2.0),
an ADDITIONAL obligation that must be satisfied as well (a conjunct), or an EXCEPTION that
modifies a grant (the operand of a WITH, e.g. LLVM-exception)?
The expression alone cannot tell you: a dual-licensed crate legitimately reproduces BOTH
texts of an OR, so reproducing a text is not evidence of conjunction. Recording the role
lets the generator check that an additional obligation is actually named in a conjunct
position rather than merely appearing somewhere in the string, that every part of a
COMPOUND cited expression holds a conjunct position, and that an exception text is
accompanied by a conjunct granted WITH it.
